summary: The following claims interpret the T10a results regarding what GRASP encodes chemically compared to baselines.

claims.claim: GRASP layer-12 mean pooling captures topological connectivity for MMP inhibition beyond Morgan fingerprint counts.
claims.evidence: SR-MMP Mean Pool L12 AUROC = 0.889 (GRASP) vs 0.756 (Morgan).
claims.test: Label column: `is_mmp_inhibitor`. Prediction: Molecules with identical Morgan fingerprints but different ring fusion topology should show higher L12 mean activation in GRASP than Random, correlating with the label.
claims.prediction: If true, filtering for isomers (same SMILES hash) will yield AUROC > 0.756 on topological variants where Morgan fails.

claims.claim: Deep layers of pretrained GRASP degrade ClinTox toxicity signal without task-specific tuning.
claims.evidence: CT_TOX Mean Pool L12 AUROC = 0.706 (GRASP) vs 0.834 (Random).
claims.test: Label column: `is_clintox_tox`. Prediction: Layer-4 mean pooling should yield higher correlation with toxicity labels than L12 if the signal is diluted at depth.
claims.prediction: If true, AUROC for CT_TOX on L4 (0.879) must remain > 0.75 while L12 drops to < 0.75.

claims.claim: Molecular weight explains a baseline portion of Androgen Receptor binding but specific functional groups are required for high performance.
claims.evidence: NR-AR-LBD Mean Pool Size AUROC = 0.694 vs GRASP L12 = 0.820.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[#7]` (Nitrogen). Prediction: Molecules with Nitrogen count > 3 should show higher GRASP activation than Random for NR-AR-LBD.
claims.prediction: If true, molecules with MW < 400 and N_count >= 3 will have AUROC contribution from size baseline near 0.69 but GRASP L12 remains high (0.82).

claims.claim: Task-specific fine-tuning (A1) improves Androgen Receptor binding prediction over raw pretrained features.
claims.evidence: NR-AR-LBD Mean Pool A1 AUROC = 0.830 vs GRASP L6 = 0.820.
claims.test: Label column: `is_ar_lbd_active`. Prediction: Precision on molecules with high TPSA (>60) should be higher for A1 than raw GRASP.
claims.prediction: If true, the subset of NR-AR-LBD positives with TPSA > 60 will have precision_A1 > precision_GRASP_raw.

claims.claim: GRASP layer depth optimizes aggregation of pharmacophores differently across targets.
claims.test: Label column: `is_mmp_inhibitor`. Prediction: Attention weights at L12 should correlate with distance between Zinc-binding group and hydrophobic tail.
claims.prediction: If true, removing the linker atoms in SMILES will drop GRASP performance more than Morgan fingerprints for MMP targets.

trivial_explanations: Size baseline (MW/Heavy Atoms) explains ~0.69-0.75 AUROC on some tasks without chemical specificity, indicating lipophilicity or steric bulk correlates with toxicity in these datasets.
Random weights outperform GRASP L12 for CT_TOX Mean Pool (0.834 vs 0.706), suggesting the pretrained representation collapses specific toxicophore signals at depth.
